source_caption:
🎬 Still Mine (2012)

Still Mine follows Craig Morrison, an elderly Canadian farmer who has spent decades building a peaceful life with his beloved wife, Irene. As Irene’s memory begins to fade and her health deteriorates, Craig becomes determined to build a smaller, safer home on their property where they can continue living together independently. Despite his experience as a skilled carpenter, Craig finds himself battling government regulations, building inspectors, and legal obstacles that threaten to stop his project. Refusing to give up, he fights to protect his wife’s dignity and the life they have built together. Based on a true story and starring James Cromwell and Geneviève Bujold, the film delivers a deeply emotional and heartwarming story about lifelong love, devotion, aging, perseverance, and the extraordinary sacrifices people make for those they love.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Romance • Biography

⭐ IMDb: 7.4/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 42m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Michael McGowan

✍️ Writer: Michael McGowan

🏆 Awards: James Cromwell won the Canadian Screen Award for Best Actor.

source_details.synopsis: Still Mine is a 2012 Canadian romantic drama film. The film had a limited release under its original title Still at the 2012 Toronto International Film Festival; it had a general release on May 3, 2013. Written and directed by Michael McGowan and based on a true story, the film stars James Cromwell as Craig Morrison, a farmer in rural St. Martins, New Brunswick who battles a government bureaucrat (Jonathan Potts) for the right to build a new house for his ailing wife Irene (Geneviève Bujold) when their existing home no longer suits her health needs. The international distribution rights were licensed by Cinema Management Group.
